Healthy, youthful, and articulate, Rama had a keen awareness of appropriate conduct and a deep understanding of people.  His exceptional qualities made him the favorite of the people, cherished like their very lifeblood.  Mastering all areas of knowledge, including the Vedas, he surpassed even his renowned father in archery and mystical weaponry.  Blessed and benevolent, Rama remained steadfast in truth and integrity. He was guided by the wisdom of learned Brahmins, developing a strong understanding of righteousness, prosperity, and worldly affairs.  Modest and discreet, he attracted many followers.  He was judicious in both rewarding and punishing, and discerning in his assessment of character.  Rama was adept at assembling and supporting virtuous individuals, strategic in the use of force, and knowledgeable in financial matters, both in generating revenue and appropriate expenditure. __data__.text: Rama approached his father, King Dasaratha, who sat dejectedly with Kaikeyi.  Rama bowed respectfully to both. Dasaratha, tearful and distressed, could barely acknowledge Rama's presence.  Observing his father's unusual state, Rama became apprehensive, like one who accidentally steps on a snake. He saw the king emaciated with grief, sighing, and looking like a turbulent ocean, a sun in eclipse, or a sage who has uttered falsehood.  Concerned, Rama wondered why his father, usually so affectionate, was unresponsive. He questioned Kaikeyi, asking if he had unknowingly offended his father and pleading with her to intervene on his behalf. He expressed his deep concern for Dasaratha's well-being, hoping he was not suffering from physical or mental anguish, and anxiously inquired if he had offended Bharata, Shatrughna, or any of his mothers. Rama declared that he could not bear to live if he had displeased his father in any way.
